records.title: Requested repetition of an assessment that negotiation participation is pointless
records.header_literal: B) ZÖN v OKM (08.14 p.m., November 18th); 1600 (11/18); 4 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-[2-like]48
records.readable_german: An OKM. Erbetene Wiederholung hiesiger RM 1 A 112?? GEH OP vom ? 11. Teilnahme an Verhandlungen gemaess dort RM 1?A 11222 OP zwecklos.
records.meaning: The first part gives the requested repetition of a locally issued reference and states that participation in negotiations, according to the cited message, is pointless. The exact reference numbers, date-like labels and scope of those negotiations remain unresolved; the statement does not establish whether negotiations occurred.
notes: All 248 native source slots are retained, including the four dashes in A---- and two dashes in FVG--. Five dash values are supplied by the readable proposal and one reference-field dash stays unresolved.

The header length digit is 2-like but imperfectly printed. The header is therefore transcribed RICHI-[2-like]48; the 248-slot body is counted independently from the source and does not erase the glyph qualification.
WIEDERHODUNG to WIEDERHOLUNG, TEWLNAHME to TEILNAHME, and the incomplete VERHANDLUNGEN/GEMAESS/DORT wording have explicit costs: three observed substitutions and five dash fills in total.
The four-part heading is retained. This edition covers the two printed parts shown here and supplies no missing part 3 or 4.
The reference-field unknown at plaintext 103 is a printed dash under pair X?, with domain {A,C,K,M,O,X}; it cannot be a numeral, while X remains a possible separator label.

B1 plaintext 45 and B2 plaintext 22 share square cell VA. B1 plaintext 46 and B2 plaintext 59/69 share GG. B1 plaintext 58 is GF; B2 plaintext 40 is GD and 41 is AF. These five distinct fully observed unknown square cells must take distinct labels from {0,3,4,5,6,7,8,9}; repeated cells must agree.

records.title: Cited messages settled by the order to depart issued locally
records.header_literal: B) ZÖN v OKM (08.14 p.m., November 18th); 1600 (11/18); 4 TEILE; 2 TL RICHI-236
records.readable_german: Dortige Nr. RM 1 A 1122? OP und RM 1 A 112?? OP und RM 1UA 112?1 OP vom ? 11 durch den hier gegebenen Abmarschbefehl erledigt.
records.meaning: The second part states that the cited messages have been dealt with by the order to depart issued locally. It records the order and its effect on the correspondence, not proof that the troops completed their departure. The literal 1UA reference and all unresolved number-like fields remain unchanged.
notes: All 236 native coordinates are visible, with no source erasures. The earlier OCR contains only 196 coordinates; restoring the omitted visible row is a source transcription correction, not a 40-coordinate historical insertion.
The two word or separator proposals are HIWR to HIER and the M after the literal date-like 11 to separator X. Each costs one observed-coordinate substitution.
1UA is retained literally, despite the nearby repeated 1A reference pattern. No numerical field is repaired to match a presumed sequence.

The five remaining ? positions arise from fully observed unknown square cells. The shared-cell and distinct-cell constraints are given with part 1 and enforced by a single injective completion witness.

prior_credit: Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier repository OCR and unchanged-key outputs are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. No universal first-decipherment priority is asserted.
limits: All native source slots remain in printed order; no insertion, deletion or reordering.
Unknown square cells remain globally coupled and injective. Roundtrip completion witnesses are explicitly nonhistorical.
Observed-coordinate substitutions and source-mask fills are priced separately. A source-compatible word proposal is not proof of unique historical wording.
